comments:
DO NOT STAY HERE. There are endless Airbnb options in Asheville such that you should avoid this one. I don't know how it got so many misleading positive reviews. We should have read through all of them for the token honest review that warned to stay away from here. This place is filthy, disgusting, and unsuitable for vacation.

All the prior reviews are misleading. The photos are misleading. There is a torn leather couch with a sheet over it. The bed was so gross I put my shirt over the pillow to put my head down. The bathroom looked like it hadn't been cleaned in a decade. I put toilet paper down as a protective layer for the toilet. The shower was filthy with mildew on everything. I showered with flip flops on.

I've traveled a lot and I by no means expect swanky accommodations. In all the Airbnb's I've stayed in, this is the worst by leaps and bounds.

Brady, the host, brags about his experience working in a 5 star resort, but he can't provide 1 star accommodations. I would be embarrassed to list this place to the public. He should be embarrassed. There were dead bugs on the towels, live bugs on the walls, spiders in and around the bed. It was terrible.

Uh, the place was kind of a let down to put it nicely. Run down and really dark/dingy. The bed was the worst. It reminded me of a college dorm room? Dark and musty. The couch smells like mildew and seemed possibly wet?

There isn't a way to control the heat/cold. That's controlled by the upstairs house, which is weirdly connected to Brady's room through a stairway that's actually accessible through a door. Meaning you could go into the above house and back from this place. That's not safe at all.

The upstairs people's friend parked in the driveway, meaning we had to ask them to move. That's not a big deal, but each time we came home late, we feared someone from upstairs would be in our 'space' and there's nowhere else to park since this place is in an alley and on a hill.

Overall, the reviews were all positive, but I think AirBnB's review system is flawed, and since I hardly use the service, I don't have a problem being honest here.

Brady wasn't a good host. I asked him for advice on where to go, and he replied with a short message - that he liked the pizza place across the street. He also said he'd be out of reach for the weekend, and if I needed something to call his friend instead. Huh?

I get the impression that Brady uses AirBnB to help him pay his rent, and whenever he can, books his place and sleeps nearby (possibly even upstairs in the house above?) No idea. But this simply isn't a great place for spending a weekend, and certainly isn't a place you'd want to spend a romantic weekend. It's about a mile from downtown, and not bike friendly at all. An Uber costs $20 each way at peak times.

Asheville itself is a great place. We enjoyed going to many artsy locations, trials and waterfalls in the area, and met a lot of great people. But for $150 a night, we could have found a cheap hotel within a short walk of downtown. At least we would have known the bed was changed recently, and would have a television in the room.

And coffee. Gotta have your coffee.

Sorry Brady. Your place needs a major overhaul. I feel bad for people who have high expectations (or even medium expectations). Either that or the standards of AirBnb have really gone downhill. If that's the case, then I'm going to be hesitant

The main selling point to this home is the location. We were within walking distance from many places and the area was really beautiful. Of course, as the description states, this place isn't exactly like a hotel so don't expect extra hotel style amenities but it is a comfortable place to stay. My only complaint is that it is not as private as described, as there is a shared laundry room that an upstairs tenant has access to, which CAN be locked but was not when we arrived. Overall, it's worth it for the location.

Brady’s place is in a great location, cheaply priced but you get what you pay for. It’s kind of outdated, there’s no TV which is specified in the listing. However, I wish I had a television to drown out the noise of the people who lived upstairs. The floors are very thin and I heard every footstep until past midnight. Bed is comfortable, wasn’t terrible but won’t be renting again.

listing_name: Basement: Mountainside Private Room & Private Bath
comments: The place was a nice value for the money...I see now the host charges $17 per guest, and I picked my sister up along the way in our road trip which is probably why the host made us feel like an inconvenience the moment we arrived. The GPS takes you in circles in the Mountains which is not their fault, but upon arriving we find tenant parking is quite a bit down the way on a steep hill. The host lives upstairs and was there the moment we checked in with an aloof demeanor. She advised us we could pull up the van closer to the house to remove our items, but I told her we were exhausted from the adventure we were on in the mountains finding the place and were going straight to bed. The next morning I pulled the van near the apartment to bring our items in which I ensured not to block anyone or entry ways, but after removing our things I went to move the van back to tenant parking and I walked up on the hosts complaining about it. Also, after we checked in and were getting settled in for bed my daughter pushed the button on the O2 alarm which we immediately shut off, but we received more aloof correspondence from the host asking us to respect the others by being quite which we were except the O2, but I get it the alarm went off for a second. HOWEVER, come 530AM the host begins to stomp excessively and as loud as she can through the top of the house and continues to do so until we leave...which would not have been an issue had she not send an aloof message asking us to respect others. Great Place, but the hosts need to work on their delivery, and if it was about $17 she could have stated so and I would have gladly given it to her instead of  being rude and making us feel like an inconvenience. Would not book again...

listing_name: Basement: Mountainside Private Room & Private Bath
comments:
On the positive side, the room had a separate entryway and was large and spacious. The bed was comfortable. The surroundings, deep in the woods, were quiet. They do keep the room quite cool overnight, in the 60s in the summer. But there was a comforter and that is a fine temperature for me. Plus they left a space heater in the room for those who need one.
On the negative side, the water pressure is very weak which I noticed the first night with my toilet backup problem. And I noticed it again on the second night. On the first night just going to the bathroom, it didn't seem to completely flush and the toilet backed-up to within an inch of overflowing.
I was afraid to touch it further, messaged the host and asked him if he could fix it while I was out next day: He said it was my fault, that I had somehow clogged the plumbing (I hadn't) and I should have used the plunger that was in the bathroom and I should be "embarrassed" for having asked him to fix the problem. I didn't mention the following at the time: I didn't see a plunger in the room, and if I had used one -- I'm not a plumbing expert, but I think those rubber things with a handle kind of push the water up and down vigorously
through suction and pressure -- you certainly don't want to do on a full toilet and all of the waste products would have probably overflowed onto the floor. ( Also, if the host didn't already realize he had some sort of a plumbing or water pressure problem, why would he leave a plunger in all his guestrooms? )
In all of my many experiences with airbnb hosts in the past, they have always been pleasant, gracious, and eager to fix any problem or answer any question. Turning that around and trying to blame on the guest something you should have fixed by hiring a plumber before you rent a room is hardly the route to take. That, and the morning I left, messaging me that I was late leaving and I should "vacate immediately" -- when I was out the door within 5 or 10 minutes of checkout time made the whole stay feel a bit unpleasant.

listing_name: Basement: Mountainside Private Room & Private Bath
comments: It was okay. It was clean, it was a place to sleep, and I was offered clean towels, a fridge, and a coffee maker. The patio is not as pictured... it now has 2 chairs and a cooler turned upside down. I was bummed about that. But I didn't mind that I had to park at the end of the driveway and carefully step as I lugged my belongings (took a few trips) up the semi-steep, rocky, wavy, unfinished driveway. I also didn't mind squeezing through the space between the staircase and the house to get to the door.. or having to put my belongings down and take them through that spot one at a time because we didn't fit together. I also didn't mind that there wasn't any soap in the bathroom (shower or sink). I mean, there was a used up hand soap bottle that had about 1/3 of an inch of a diluted mixture that was mostly water. But that was okay, because I had a bar of soap in my toiletry kit. I also didn't mind that I could hear every foot step as the hosts moved about their home above my head... instead I found myself hoping my movements weren't as audible to them. I also didn't mind that it took 3 blankets to stay warm or mind reading the note that said I had no control over the temperature but I should be fine because they offered extra blankets. And it's true, I was fine with it. Truly, all of these little things were okay, but putting them all together, I kinda felt like a second class citizen. I mean, even that's okay.. its not like I'm a family member or an invited guest in their home. I'm just some stranger sleeping in their basement.

listing_name: Basement: Mountainside Private Room & Private Bath
comments:
We were excited about booking this room, but I was very disappointed with the bed. It sags both right to left, and head to foot, with the lowest part being in the center. I woke up with a backache long before daylight. I finally moved to the sofa at 5:00 a.m. The sofa didn't hurt my back. The second night, I tried to sleep on the other side of the bed, hoping that might be better. It wasn't quite as bad on the side of the bed closest to the exterior door, but it still gave me a backache and I moved to the sofa again before daylight. I didn't try to sleep on this bed for the final two nights we were there. I should add that we often stay in budget-minded accommodations when we travel, and I have never had this experience before. For me, the baseline for a place to stay away from home is a comfortable bed, and I have never felt a need to voice a concern for the comfort of a bed before. Soft or firm, beds haven't been a big deal to me before. But this sagging one was a problem for me. Evidently, from reading other reviews, others actually like this bed. It just didn't work well for me, and I felt people should be aware that the bed sags.
That said, there are many things to like about this place. The large open room, great Internet, and very quiet and peaceful location are pluses.
Another thing that may be a concern for some people is that the window only has a sheer. No blinds or curtain to block morning light or add privacy. We went to town and purchased a paper drop cloth to cover the window and that significantly blocked morning light coming in while we were trying to sleep.
If you stay here, you may want to consider taking your valuables out of the room when you are not there, since there is not a way to lock the door to the upstairs guests or the garage, and the overhead garage door was left open for long periods while we were there.

BEWARE OF ANTS (and other issues)
TLDR Summary:
While the property is adorable and in a great part of Asheville, we did not feel the host properly warned of or responded to the significant ant issue we experienced during our first 12 hours in the property. We also had a few other issues with the property that are noted at the end of the review. We ended up vacating the property in favor of a hotel after that 1st night (rather than staying 3 more nights as initially booked).
Details:
I’ll preface this review by sharing that I’ve stayed in 22 different Airbnbs over the past 7 years (including two other trips to Asheville, one of which was in the same neighborhood as this property during the same time of year) and have always had very positive experiences. Unfortunately on our recent July 2021 trip to Asheville, this was not the case. Upon arrival, we noticed a few concerns (listed at the end of the review) but experienced our major issue when we woke up around 7:30am the next morning after less than 12 hours in the property.

We woke up to find the kitchen infested with ants, including ants all over/in the brand new, unopened package of muffins we’d bought at the grocery store the next before. We messaged the host immediately about the ant issue and she got back to us about 90 minutes later with the following response “Yikes! They will find a way in regardless of the seal of the door. Ants are very common in town this time of year. I’ll get some Terro before heading to work in about an hour. I’m out currently, but it will work by itself just fine. Moving forward I suggest storing items away in the cupboard and not leaving open food on the counters. Those muffin packages are not sealed. If you have not done so, I’d put everything they’ve infected in the trash and on the porch outside, and they will dissipate when there isn’t anything for them to get. Once the Terro is in place their presence will be very minimal.” She then responded back about an hour later as follows “I left ant bait outside your door. You’ll also find some cotton balls. They have essential oil on them and those are to put near your food in the corners on the counter. A safer alternative for food safe areas. You can use all four traps in the box. One on each side on the door inside. I’d also put one in the bathroom, and the other where you see fit. I have to head to work now, but if y’all are planning to be gone all day, I can prep the space for you when I get back around 2.”
As you can see in her response, the host noted that ants are a common issue and that we should be storing the food in particular ways & places, however she never disclosed any of this in either the Airbnb listing or in the check-in instructions (and we’ve never had issues with ants on either of our prior visits to Asheville, which included a stay in the same neighborhood at the same time of year). If this is a common issue, I’d expect the host to (1) disclose this at least prior to check-in so guests can plan accordingly and (2) provide airtight storage options to guests (Tupperware, Ziploc bags, etc.) – but this was not the case. She left the ant traps and loose cotton balls with essential oil on them outside the front door for us to deal with, rather than entering the property to address the ants herself. She also recommended we put an ant trap in the bathroom, which is on the other side of the bedroom from the kitchen, which made us very concerned that ants could now be expected throughout the property and therefore get into our clothing and other belongings. And while the cost of the muffins was minimal, there wasn’t even an offer to reimburse us for them despite the ant issue making them inedible.
Other issues:
1) SAFETY CONCERN – there are two windows in the TV room that cannot be locked at all. We were surprised by this as we’d always thought all Airbnbs had to have working locks on doors and windows.
2) Differences from property listing (amenities, layout, etc.)
a) The fridge was substantially smaller than noted in the listing’s photos (it’s now a mini fridge). The larger fridge was one of the things that factored into our initial decision to stay in the property, so we were disappointed that it was much smaller than advertised.
b) The bed is configured differently from the listing’s photos so, if more than one person is sleeping in the bed, it requires a person to sleep next to the wall/windows and crawl in/out of the end of the bed or crawl over the other person. This bed setup also means there isn’t easy access to either nightstand.
3) The parking pass was broken and could not be hung on the rearview mirror as advised in the check-in instructions. We contacted the host to confirm that we could leave the parking pass on our dashboard.
4) The toilet seat won’t stay up. Just a heads up if male guest(s) are staying in this property.
